sections.title: About the Lab
content: The Smart Grid and Sustainable Energy Transition Lab was established to respond to the rapid transformation of electricity systems driven by renewable energy integration, digital technologies and decarbonization goals. The lab serves as a platform for applied research, system analysis, pilot studies, and capacity development in the power and energy sector.

Operating within the academic environment of MIST, the lab integrates theoretical research with practical implementation, emphasizing solutions that are technically sound, economically viable, and policy-relevant.

domains.title: Thematic Research Domains and Focus Areas

cards.title: Smart Grids, Digitalization, and Power System Intelligence
cards.text: Research on smart grid technologies, digital power systems, and cyber-physical infrastructures, including advanced sensing, communication, automation, and AI-driven monitoring and control.

cards.title: Renewable Energy, Energy Storage, and Electric Mobility
cards.text: Integration of renewable energy, energy storage systems, and electric vehicle infrastructure with power grids to enhance flexibility, reliability, and decarbonization.

cards.title: Energy Efficiency, Demand Side Management
cards.text: Development of energy efficiency measures, demand-side management, and demand response strategies to optimize energy use, reduce peak demand, and improve system performance.

cards.title: Power System Planning and Operation
cards.text: Analysis of long-term planning, real-time operation, and resilience of power systems under technical, economic, and climate-related uncertainties.

sections.title: Mission & Vision
content: To become an international research center in smart grid and sustainable energy research, contributing to resilient, secure, and low-carbon power systems at national and regional levels.
# Conduct high-quality research on smart grids and sustainable energy systems
# Support energy transition and energy security through evidence-based analysis
# Strengthen industry–academia collaboration in power and energy sectors
# Train future engineers and researchers with practical, future-ready skills
# Contribute to national and global energy and climate goals
